evidence: Ov. M. 13.790: longā prōcērior alnō (Lewis & Short)
Suet. Vesp. 23: homō prōcērae statūrae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Tall and slender: of people, necks and trees (Cicero’s prōcērissimae populī, Leg. 1.15). To ask how tall someone is, Latin asks about statūra, height: quā statūrā (Cic. Phil. 2.41, below).

evidence: Ov. M. 3.181: altior illīs ipsa dea est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: High, of whatever rises, seen from below: walls, trees, mountains; less often of people. It also means deep (seen from above), and of the mind lofty (Lewis & Short; see height).

evidence: Publ. Syr. E 16: Excelsīs multō facilius cāsus nocet.
terms.comment: High up, towering, and so eminent, noble (animus excelsus, Cic.; Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: velim mihi dīcās, L. Turselius quā faciē fuerit, quā statūrā
phrases.english: I should like you to tell me what Lucius Turselius looked like and how tall he was

phrases.latin: corporaque eōrum inprōcēra fierī minusque adolēscere
phrases.english: and their bodies stay short and grow up less

phrases.latin: Redīstī prōcērior. — At equidem māllem prūdentior, aut doctior.
phrases.english: You’ve come back taller! — I’d rather have come back wiser, or more learned.
phrases.source: Erasm. Coll., Fōrm., Percontandī dē valētūdine, I 12

phrases.english: to be a head taller than
he is taller by a whole head
phrases.source: Verg. A. 7.784 (Lewis & Short s.v. vertex); Traupman 326
